summary: A whole monthly VPS plan per fixed size, paid one month or one year in advance; the plan bills whether the server runs or is stopped, and the only hourly meter is a pay-as-you-go product new accounts cannot buy.

egress.included: 1 TB on Nano, 2 TB on XS, 5 TB on SM, 10 TB on MED, 20 TB on LG, 32 TB on XL and XXL, per month, inbound and outbound counted together
egress.note: There is no per-GiB overage rate. The monthly allowance is a hard cap: when it is used up the server cannot be started or restarted until you buy more capacity or the next period begins. Extra capacity is sold in 1 TB steps at 10 SEK (about $1.17) per TB per month, up to 500 TB. Not priced by the calculator.

plans.name: Monthly plan
plans.note: One plan per server per month. The same plan can be paid for 12 months at 10% off, in which case the whole year is charged upfront.

notes: Currency: HostUp bills in SEK, EUR or USD. These USD figures are HostUp's own USD display on 2026-10-30, not a market rate: the chain is the SEK list price divided by 10 for EUR (49 SEK to 4.90 EUR) and that EUR figure times 7/6 for USD (4.90 EUR to $5.72). The SEK list prices are 35, 49, 99, 199, 399, 749 and 1,499 a month.

VAT: HostUp's own pages disagree. Its price calculator shows a subtotal marked excl. VAT with a 25% VAT line under it; its cart labels the same total inc. VAT. The card follows the calculator and treats these figures as ex-VAT: a private customer in Sweden would then add 25% (VPS XS $5.72 becomes $7.15), a private customer elsewhere in the EU their own rate, while a VAT-registered business in another EU country and a customer outside the EU pay the figure shown. If the cart label is the literal one, the published figure already includes VAT and every total here is 25% too high for a business buyer.

Annual term: 10% off the monthly price, paid for the whole year upfront. In USD that is $44.10, $61.72, $124.72, $250.72, $502.72, $943.72 and $1,888.72 a year, or $3.68 to $157.39 a month. The monthly price is the ongoing month-to-month price, not an introductory rate.

A stopped standard VPS keeps billing in full: the plan is a subscription for the period and the disk stays. Stopping is a power-off, so memory and running processes are lost. There is no pause and no cheaper stopped rate on this product.

Hourly pay-as-you-go Cloud VMs exist but are gated: the account needs identity verification (passport, ID card or Swedish BankID) and at least SEK 2,000 of paid invoices first. Their per-hour rates are shown only inside the client area, so they are not modelled here.

Disk and bandwidth can be raised on any plan: extra NVMe at 0.55 SEK (about $0.06) per GB a month up to 5,000 GB on the slider, extra bandwidth at 10 SEK (about $1.17) per TB a month. CPU and memory only change by moving to another plan, which restarts the server. The calculator charges extra disk as disk.extraMonthly at $0.0642 per GiB a month (0.55 SEK at the same display conversion); HostUp bills it as more disk on the same server, not as a separate volume, and it is bought for a whole month.

CPU is allocated to the guest but not permanently dedicated: a server that has run at full load for several days is capped at 50% of its vCPUs, and heavy disk I/O can be throttled temporarily. A, B and C sit far below that.

The primary public IPv4 is included. Extra IPv4 addresses, kept reserved addresses and the one-time private-network fee are charged, but their prices appear only in the client area and are not modelled.

Snapshots are included in plan slots and deleted after 24 hours. Backups are included, weekly by default, with seven slots on the smallest plan; extra slots cost 1 SEK (about $0.12) a month each. Neither has a separate storage rate.
Windows Server is bring-your-own-licence; the licence is not in the price.
